raw_response:
I am old now, and I do not gamble much. What I do is mostly what has worked on my land before. Wheat and maize still keep the house steady, and cotton gives me some cash if the price is not too bad. I have 15 mu total, and I will keep most of the land in wheat-maize because that is the safest for us. I will leave 5 mu in cotton, because I know how to grow it and I have a well if it turns dry. Money must be watched. Some people in the family work outside, so labor at home is not enough for too much hand work, so I keep the plan simple and close to what we can manage.

For the wheat land, I will use 10 mu and then plant maize on the same 10 mu right after wheat harvest. I do not want to cut fertilizer too hard, because if wheat or maize turns yellow, the loss is bigger than the savings. But I also will not chase very high yield. Cotton I keep lighter on fertilizer than wheat-maize, and I will only spray when I really see trouble. Water from the well costs money, so I will irrigate at the key times, not too many times.
